notes: Hand-written golden scenarios for the G01 membership engine (docs/contracts/g01.md). Every expectation in 'scenarios' was worked out by hand from the contract before either implementation produced it; none was read back from the model or from the Rust.

tests/g01/reference.py is the independent Python model that replays them. The Rust engine replays the same file only under the centralized builds; until a Rust replay exists this file is evidence about the model and the contract, not about franken-session.

Ops: quorum, found, observe, request, raw_request, respond, gather, round_start/round_ack/round_outcome, record, restart, restore, forget (voters); node, issue, live, renew, assume, adopt, session, probe, advance, discover, gate, grant_output, permitted (engine); propose, ack, commit, abort, tick, status, resolve, start_gate, unresolved, restart_node (cutover); repeat expands its steps count times with "$n" counting from 1.

An expectation is {ok: {...}} (every named key must equal the result) or {error: CODE, details: {...}} (the stable code, and the named numbers of the refusal). Times are [ns, frame] for engine calls and plain ns for voters.

The 'plants' section is model output too: for each fault planted in the DRIVER of the engine (zero_uncertainty: the margin forced to 0; early_voter_clock: every voter judged at a far-future clock; flipped_policy: the missing-acknowledgement policy swapped; flipped_mint: the epoch-minting mode swapped) the scenarios the model says it breaks. A replay that applies the same plant to the real engine must break exactly those, and it must break at least one.

The 'schedule' section is the exception to hand-written: its counts are the model's output for the seeded partition schedule in crates/franken-session/src/membership.rs (same SplitMix64 and draw order), kept so a Rust replay can be compared with them exactly. tests/g01/reference.py --check refuses any drift.

scenarios.title: a join changes nothing audible until its cutover frame, then activates exactly once
a leave removes the member only at its cutover frame
a token that is not current is refused by every mutation and changes nothing
a commit under a stale epoch is refused because the epoch advance aborted the proposal
a missing acknowledgement blocks the commit, then the deadline aborts without holding the group
an unreachable member is excluded, the cutover continues, and its output stays unresolved
an unreachable joiner aborts even when unreachable members are excluded
duplicate acknowledgements are idempotent, a different one conflicts, strangers and late calls are refused
no new acknowledgement is accepted at or after the deadline
commit refuses a member that is not ready, a cutover before an output tail, and a cutover already reached
cancelling a committed join before its frame leaves the group untouched
an uncommitted proposal lapses when its cutover frame arrives
one change at a time, and every precondition is checked before anything is recorded
a group of two at its maximum refuses a third member
after a restart no mutation is accepted until authority is rediscovered
settled results are kept for reconciliation, but only the last 64
a renewal needs a majority, so a minority cannot extend a lease
an even electorate splits into a refusal, never a tie, and a voter cannot be completed for the rival
five voters need three; two acknowledgements are not enough
a single voter is its own quorum
acknowledgements must match the open request, a repeat counts once, and a late quorum is no quorum
a takeover waits for the conservative expiry and is granted to one candidate for the next epoch only
a voter that has seen no lease cannot judge expiry and grants nothing
the holder stops u before its lease ends and a taker is granted only u after it
the voter in both quorums orders them: a takeover granted first refuses the late renewal
the voter in both quorums orders them: a renewal acknowledged first delays the takeover
two candidates cannot both win an epoch
a voter extends only a lease it knows to be the requester's and learns only forward
a partitioned holder cannot renew, the majority takes over, and the old holder is fenced when it hears
adopting a newer epoch aborts the proposal in flight and fences an unexpired stale token
when a lease lapses, granted output plays out to its frame and nothing new is issued
a voter without its durable record refuses everything until it is restored; a voter that forgot grants the rival
a group mints epochs by one rule only, and a restarted node must learn the holder first
a quorum result applies only to the token and session it was gathered for
a quorum is a strict majority of the electorate, and an electorate must name a voter
a token flawed in two ways is refused by the first condition in the contract's order: group, stale, future, issuer, expiry
PLANTED: with no margin and a holder clock 40 ns slow, two leaders hold a live lease at once
with u = 19 the overlap shrinks to two instants
with u = 20 the same skew leaves no overlap
with u = 50 the holder is dead from true time 990 and the taker starts at 1050
